questions.stem: Which Resource Profile can be used to define when start and stop a resource?
questions.explanation: The Schedule Profile defines when to start and stop a resource. It lets administrators specify the days of the week and times of day when a stack should be started, stopped, or deprovisioned. Security Profiles and Lease Profiles are not real CPG resource profile types. Application Profiles install software on provisioned resources, not control timing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for a Compute Profile? (Choose two.)

options.text: Defines what virtual hardware is presented to end users
Defines custom t-shirt sizes (small, medium, large, etc.) for virtual hardware
Defines OS choices for Cloud Catalog offerings
Defines when virtual hardware can be provisioned by end users

questions.explanation: A Compute Profile specifies the virtual hardware for newly-provisioned VMs, including virtual CPUs, memory, and local storage (A). It also defines custom t-shirt sizes like Micro, Small, Medium, and Large that map to specific hardware configurations (B). OS choices belong to OS Profiles (C), Security Group offerings to Compute Security Group Profiles (D), and provisioning schedules to Schedule Profiles (E).

questions.stem: Which Permission would you use to make a Catalog Item for a cloud native application that you plan to release, viewable but not executable, for users who belong to the Marketing Developers group?
questions.explanation: The Access permission (also called Read) allows users to see a record but not edit, delete, or execute it. This makes a catalog item viewable but not executable. Execute permission would allow running actions, All grants full permissions, and 'Viewer' is not a real CPG permission type. The five permission types in CPG are: Access [Read], Manage [Create & Update], Delete, Execute, and All.

questions.stem: What governance objects are available in Cloud Provisioning and Governance? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Cloud Governance in CPG provides four types of governance objects: Quotas (A), Policies (C), Pools, and Permissions (D). Quotas limit resource usage, Policies control approvals and override settings system-wide, and Permissions define group-level access rights. Credentials (B) are authentication objects, not governance, and SLAs (E) are not a CPG governance type.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes what Puppet, Chef, Ansible Tower and Salt are utilized for?
questions.explanation: Puppet, Chef, Ansible Tower, and Salt are all configuration management tools. CPG integrates with these continuous delivery (configuration management) providers to install and manage software on provisioned resources. They are not used for cost control (A), cloud monitoring (C), or continuous integration (D). Ansible is the default supported provider in CPG.

questions.stem: Cloud Scripts and Cloud Script Templates utilize which host based scripting tools to install software?
questions.explanation: Cloud Script Templates in CPG are actual executables passed to target VMs for execution. They can be Shell scripts, PowerShell scripts, or CloudInit scripts depending on the execution context. The other options list languages (Ruby, JavaScript, Perl) that are not used as host-based Cloud Script Template types in CPG. Cloud Scripts themselves use JavaScript for platform-side logic, but the templates that execute on VMs use Shell and PowerShell.

questions.stem: How are variables grouped for a Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: Variable Sets are used to group variables for a Service Catalog item. In CPG, catalog items for cloud templates use variable sets to organize cloud-related variables into logical groups. Each variable set appears as a tab on the catalog item's order form, allowing users to fill in grouped parameters (e.g., network settings, compute settings) separately.

questions.stem: What must be created in Azure before you can configure Azure Alerts in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Before configuring Azure Alerts in ServiceNow CPG, you must first create a Monitor Alert rule in Azure. Azure Monitor provides alerting capabilities that generate alerts based on metrics and activity logs. A Network Security Group (A) manages firewall rules, a Resource Group (B) organizes resources, and an App Service (C) hosts web apps. The alert integration requires the Azure Monitor Alert to exist so ServiceNow can receive and process the alert notifications.

questions.stem: What application can you use in the Cloud Admin Portal to guide your organization through the process of setting up Cloud Provisioning and Governance?
questions.explanation: Guided Setup is the application in the Cloud Admin Portal that walks administrators through setting up Cloud Provisioning and Governance. It provides a step-by-step wizard for configuring cloud accounts, credentials, discovery, and other required components. Cloud Orchestration (A) handles workflow automation, Configuration Templates (B) are not the setup mechanism, and Cloud Planner (C) is not a real CPG application.

questions.stem: Which Cloud Provider feature do organizations depend on to provide visibility into resource management and billing? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Tags (D) and Billing Data (B) are the cloud provider features organizations depend on for resource management and billing visibility. Tags categorize cloud resources with key:value metadata that enables detailed tracking and billing reports from multiple perspectives. Billing Data provides the actual cost information. Security Groups (A) handle firewall rules, and Identity and Authentication Management (C) controls access, neither is specifically about resource management and billing.

questions.stem: IT has implemented a new poet identification code, and they would like to be able to analyze cloud consumption based upon this code. What features would you use in Cloud Provisioning and Governance to implement this request? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add a new Project Tag to the Tag Definitions
Create a Resource Pool associated to the projects table
Add new parameter to the CAPI interface

questions.explanation: To track cloud consumption by a new project identification code, you need to: (A) add a new Project Tag to the Tag Definitions so the code becomes part of resource metadata for billing analysis, and (E) manually create a new variable since the tag's value type can be set to Variable, presenting users with input on the order form. Resource Pools (B) filter tables, Cloud Scripts (C) install software, and the CAPI interface (D) handles cloud provider communication.

questions.stem: The Manager of the Marketing team wants to have control over the Cloud Resources provisioned through Cloud Provisioning and Governance. What feature in Cloud Provisioning and Governance should you use to satisfy this request?
questions.explanation: An Approval Policy is the CPG feature that gives a manager control over cloud resources provisioned by their team. Cloud Policies can create approval tasks as one of their actions, enabling system-wide control over approvals for resource operations and catalog item requests. Management Request (A), Governance Rule (B), and Policy Action Script (C) are not standard CPG features for approval workflows. The Approval Policy enforces review before resources are deployed.

questions.stem: What mechanism can be used by Cloud Provisioning and Governance to abstract vendor-specific cloud resources from end users?
questions.explanation: Resource Profiles abstract vendor-specific cloud resources from end users. They define standardized resource categories (Compute, OS, Schedule, Application, Compute Security Group) that map to different cloud providers' native offerings. Users select from profiles without needing to know provider-specific details. Policies (A) enforce governance rules, Workflows (B) automate processes, and Templates (C) are catalog item specifications, none of which serve the abstraction purpose.

questions.stem: What AWS services must be configured for Cloud Provisioning and Governance to receive alerts from AWS? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: To receive alerts from AWS in CPG, you must configure AWS SNS Topic (B) and AWS CloudWatch (E). CloudWatch monitors resources and generates alerts based on metrics and thresholds, while SNS (Simple Notification Service) delivers the alert notifications to ServiceNow. AWS CloudTrail (A) logs API calls, AWS Control Tower (C) manages multi-account governance, and AWS Config (D) evaluates resource configurations. The alerting pipeline is: CloudWatch detects → SNS delivers → ServiceNow receives.

questions.stem: Which object is rendered as a tab on the request form of a Cloud Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: A Variable Set is rendered as a tab on the request form of a Cloud Catalog Item. Variable Sets group related variables together and display as separate tabs on service catalog forms, organizing the ordering experience. Tab Set (A), Tab Group (B), and Variable Group (C) are not standard ServiceNow objects that render as tabs on catalog request forms. Variable Sets are a core Service Catalog concept used extensively in CPG catalog items.

questions.stem: For Cloud Provisioning and Governance in the Orlando release or later, where can you utilize an Application Profile?
questions.explanation: In Orlando and later, Application Profiles are utilized in Blueprints stage operations. The configuration management integration uses application profiles within blueprint operations like BootstrapNode, RegisterNode, and ExecuteConfigPackages to install software on provisioned VMs. While blueprints are in restricted usage from Orlando (no new ones can be created), existing blueprints and their application profiles continue to work. Server side includes (A) and MID Server script includes (B) serve different purposes, and post-provision operations (D) use Ansible jobs directly.

questions.stem: What would you review to quickly determine which group is deploying the most stacks?
questions.explanation: The Cloud Operations Dashboard breaks down cloud service requests and stacks from end users. Stacks are shown grouped by datacenters, and requests are broken down by requester. This dashboard (Operate > Cloud Operations Dashboard) gives a quick visual of which groups are deploying the most stacks. Cloud Activities (B) shows individual operations, not aggregate deployment stats. Cloud Request Items (C) lists individual requests without the visual grouping. The Orchestration Trail (D) tracks workflow execution steps, not deployment summaries.

questions.stem: What feature of CPG supports the use of Quotas for Templates?
questions.explanation: Cloud Policies in CPG support the enforcement of Quotas on templates. CPG has four governance types: Quotas, Policies, Pools, and Permissions. Policies act as the mechanism that enforces quota limits on template ordering, controlling how many resources or stacks a user or group can provision through a template.

questions.stem: When designing an ARM or CFT backed Catalog Item, how can you ensure that the Order Form variable automatically presents with a list of appropriate CIs from the ServiceNow CMDB?
questions.explanation: Expressions in CPG dynamically compute values for catalog item variables and resource block attributes. When designing an ARM or CFT backed catalog item, you can create an expression that queries a CMDB table (e.g., cmdb_ci_server) and uses the results to populate the order form variable with a list of appropriate CIs. Mappings (B) connect form variables to template parameters but don't query the CMDB. Conditions (C) filter when something applies. Metadata (D) provides static descriptive information.

questions.stem: After ingesting a new version of a Template, what can be done to ensure that the Order Form reflects the changes that were introduced in the new version of the Template?

options.text: Modify the Catalog Item’s Cloud Variables
Deactivate and activate the Catalog Item

questions.explanation: After ingesting a new version of a cloud template (ARM, CFT, Terraform), you must activate the template version to ensure the catalog item's order form reflects the new changes. Simply refreshing the browser or modifying variables won't pull in the new template parameters. Template versions are managed independently, and each must be explicitly activated to become the active version used by the catalog item.

questions.stem: What feature or product capability must be utilized to gather credentials for a post provisioning operation?
questions.explanation: Response processors in CPG are used to gather credentials and other data from cloud provider API responses after provisioning operations. After a VM or resource is provisioned, the response processor parses the cloud provider's REST API response to extract credentials (e.g., IP addresses, login info) and updates the CMDB with the provisioned resource details.

questions.stem: A customer on the New York release of CPG currently uses Blueprints to deploy Azure VMs. What deployment options are available to the customer when they upgrade to the latest release of CPG? (Choose two.)

options.text: Customers cannot upgrade from New York

questions.explanation: Starting with Orlando, new blueprints cannot be created in CPG, though existing ones from prior releases still work. The modern deployment options are cloud templates: Azure ARM Templates (D) and Terraform Config files (F). Jenkins Workflow (A) is not a CPG deployment mechanism. The Azure Blueprint Service (B) is an Azure-native feature, not a CPG deployment option. Puppet Manifest (C) is for configuration management, not VM deployment. Customers can upgrade from New York (E is wrong) — their existing blueprints continue working.

questions.stem: How can the required parameters for a CAPI Operation be determined?

options.text: The Cloud Provider documentation and testing
Reference the parameters used by another CAPI Operation

questions.explanation: CAPI (Cloud API) operations wrap cloud provider REST APIs to enable communication between ServiceNow and cloud services. The required parameters for each CAPI operation depend on what the underlying cloud provider API expects. Therefore, you must consult the Cloud Provider's own documentation and perform testing to determine the correct parameters. Referencing other CAPI operations (B) may give hints but parameters differ across operations. ECMA script docs (C) cover JavaScript, not cloud APIs. ServiceNow docs (D) describe CAPI framework architecture, not provider-specific API parameters.

questions.stem: When creating a new CAPI API, what is the suggested starting version number to prevent conflicts with out-of-the-box CAPI APIs?
questions.explanation: When creating a new custom CAPI API, the suggested starting version number is 2.0. This prevents version conflicts with out-of-the-box (OOB) CAPI APIs that use version 1.x. Starting at 2.0 ensures your custom API doesn't clash with existing OOB API definitions and allows clear differentiation between default and custom CAPI extensions.

questions.stem: What type of script is required for executing code to make a REST API call for a CAPI Operation?
questions.explanation: MID Server Script Includes are required to execute code that makes REST API calls for CAPI Operations. CAPI operations run on the MID Server, which acts as a proxy between the ServiceNow instance and cloud provider APIs. CAPI Method Mappers create MID Server script includes that contain the actual REST call logic for each cloud operation.

questions.stem: Which JavaScript Class can be used to make a REST API call to AWS with the least amount of code?
questions.explanation: AmazonWebServicesAPIInvoker is a purpose-built JavaScript class in ServiceNow CPG that simplifies making REST API calls to AWS. It provides high-level abstraction over AWS authentication (signing, credentials) and request construction, requiring the least amount of code compared to lower-level base classes like CloudAPIBase or AWSCloudAPIBase.

questions.stem: What CI Class Type attribute is required by Cloud Provisioning and Governance to determine uniqueness?
questions.explanation: CPG uses the object_id attribute on CI Class Types to determine uniqueness of cloud resources in the CMDB. The identification rule specifies an Object ID, and whenever components refer to a specific cloud resource, they need the Object ID to find the correct record. CI uniqueness is determined by the combination of service account, object_id, and datacenter/location, processed by the IRE. sys_id (A) is a system-generated unique key for all records, not cloud-specific. name (B) is not guaranteed unique. correlation_id (D) is for event correlation, not CI identification.

questions.stem: What Resource Block component is used to organize the Methods required to perform an Operation?
questions.explanation: Steps are the Resource Block component that organizes the Methods required to perform an Operation. Each operation requires one or more steps to do the actual work. Each step calls a specific CAPI interface and method. You can add multiple steps to a single operation, and output attributes pass values between steps. Method blocks (A) is not a real CPG component. Bindings (C) are connections between adjacent resource blocks (horizontal connections). Endpoint operations (D) is not a recognized resource block component.

questions.stem: Which three CAPI components must be configured to create a CAPI Extension?

options.text: CAPI Vendor, CAPI Interface, and CAPI REST API
CAPI Product, CAPI Method, and CAPI API
CAPI Vendor, CAPI Interface, and CAPI API
CAPI Provider, CAPI Interface, and CAPI API

questions.explanation: Creating a CAPI Extension requires three components: a CAPI Provider (defines the cloud vendor), a CAPI Interface (defines the operations/methods and parameters), and a CAPI API (ties the product and interface together with actual code, including method mappers and config overrides). The hierarchy is Provider > Products > Interfaces > APIs. Option A uses 'REST API' instead of 'API'. Option B uses 'Product' and 'Method' which are not the three core extension components. Option C says 'Vendor' instead of 'Provider' — the documentation uses 'Provider' as the correct term.

questions.stem: When testing a REST API, you receive status code of 200 from the Cloud Service. What does this mean?

options.text: A value of 200 is not a valid code
The call resulted in a server error
The call resulted in a client error

questions.explanation: HTTP status code 200 means the API call was successful (OK). This is a standard HTTP response code indicating the request was received, understood, and processed correctly. Status code 200 is definitely valid (B is wrong). Server errors use 5xx codes like 500 Internal Server Error (C is wrong). Client errors use 4xx codes like 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found (D is wrong). When testing CAPI REST calls, a 200 response confirms the cloud service accepted and processed the request.

questions.stem: When authoring a new CAPI Extension, what must you create to define the operations that will be available for the new cloud service?
questions.explanation: When authoring a CAPI Extension, you create a CAPI Interface to define the operations (methods) and parameters available for the new cloud service. Interfaces define the framework for REST calls and are reusable across different products. A CAPI Provider (A) defines the cloud vendor, not operations. A CAPI API (B) ties a product and interface together with implementation code, but the operations themselves are defined in the interface. A CAPI Product (D) categorizes resource types under a provider but doesn't define operations.

questions.stem: Before you can author a new Resource Block, what information do you require about the Host Resource Block that the Resource Block you are authoring will connect to?
questions.explanation: Before authoring a new Resource Block, you need to know the Host Interface of the host Resource Block it will connect to. In CPG, resource blocks have three interface types: guest interface (connects upward to parent), host interface (connects downward to children), and bindings (connect adjacent blocks). Your new block's guest interface connects to the host's host interface, so you must know its specification.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a supported expression type in a Resource Block?
questions.explanation: Regular Expressions are NOT a supported expression type in a Resource Block. CPG Resource Blocks support three expression types: Runtime Expressions (evaluated at request time), Complex Expressions (combine multiple values/calculations), and Definitional Expressions (define static or template-based values). Regular Expressions are a pattern-matching concept unrelated to resource block attribute resolution.

questions.stem: Which CAPI components must be configured for a Day-2 CAPI Operation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: For a Day-2 CAPI Operation (post-provisioning operations like Stop, Start, Modify), you must configure a CAPI API and a CAPI Method. The CAPI API contains the integration code and ties a product to an interface, while the CAPI Method maps to the specific operation within that API. The Provider and Interface are defined at a higher level and don't need per-operation configuration.

questions.stem: When using a CFT or an ARM Template what feature of Cloud Provisioning and Governance is used to deploy software?
questions.explanation: Cloud Scripts are used to deploy software when working with CFT or ARM Templates. Cloud script templates can be Shell, PowerShell, or CloudInit executables that run on provisioned VMs to install and configure software. OS Profiles (A) specify the operating system image, not software deployment. Compute Profiles (C) define hardware specifications like CPU, memory, and storage. Blueprints (D) are deprecated from Orlando and are infrastructure deployment templates, not specifically for software installation on top of templates.

questions.stem: When a custom workflow is called by a resource block operation, what activity should be used to get information about the operation from the Cloud Provisioning and Governance application?
questions.explanation: The Cloud Operation Context activity is used in a custom workflow called by a resource block operation to retrieve information about the triggering operation. This activity provides the workflow with context data including operation parameters, resource block details, stack information, and any input attributes needed to process the cloud operation within the workflow.

questions.stem: What API does Cloud Provisioning and Governance utilize to add and update entries in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: CPG uses the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) to add and update entries in the CMDB. The IRE processes CI data using identification rules that specify object_id, service account, and datacenter to determine uniqueness. When CAPI response processors return cloud resource data, the IRE reconciles it with existing CMDB records — creating new CIs or updating existing ones. CMDBTransformUtil (B) is for transform map operations. CMDBGroupAPI (C) is for CI group management. CI Reconciliation API (D) is not the standard term — IRE is the correct ServiceNow API.

questions.stem: Which role should be utilized for cloud alerts?
questions.explanation: The sn_cmp.cloud_event_integration role is specifically designed for cloud alert integration. This role allows the integration user or service account to receive, process, and route cloud events and alerts from external sources like AWS CloudWatch or Azure Monitor into ServiceNow. Cloud Governor (A) manages governance policies. Cloud Operator (B) handles day-to-day cloud operations and the operations dashboard. Cloud Administrator (C) has broad admin capabilities but is not the specific role for alert integration.

questions.stem: What are the three available Tag Types in Tag Management?
questions.explanation: The three available Tag Types in Tag Management are ServiceNow, Internal, and User-defined. ServiceNow tags are the system-provided default tags (like Application, Business Service, Cost Center). Internal tags are generated by the platform automatically. User-defined tags are imported from cloud providers during cloud discovery. Cloud admins can convert User-defined tags to ServiceNow (Custom) type to enable them in the Billing Dashboard. Options A and C include 'External' or 'Custom Tags' which are not the correct tag type field values. Option B lists cloud provider names, not tag types.

questions.stem: In AWS, the region-specific containers for virtual resources are called regions. In Cloud Provisioning and Governance, regions are called what?
questions.explanation: In Cloud Provisioning and Governance, AWS regions are represented as Logical Datacenters. ServiceNow uses the concept of Logical Datacenters to abstract cloud provider geographic regions/zones into a platform-neutral model. When cloud resources are discovered or provisioned, they are mapped to Logical Datacenters that correspond to the cloud provider's regions.

questions.stem: When working with Azure any service that is used must be associated with a _______________?
questions.explanation: In Azure, every service or resource must be associated with a Subscription. Subscriptions are the billing and management boundary in Azure — they link resources to an Azure account for cost tracking and access control. Without a subscription, you cannot create or use any Azure resource. Diagnostic Logs (B) are optional monitoring configurations. A Storage Account (C) is a specific resource type, not a universal requirement. Tags (D) are optional metadata. An Availability Set (E) is used for high availability of VMs, not a universal resource requirement.

questions.stem: The Azure Resource Manager uses what to organize the cloud resources required to deploy a VM?
questions.explanation: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) uses Resource Groups to organize the cloud resources required to deploy a VM. A Resource Group is a logical container that holds related Azure resources (VMs, disks, NICs, NSGs) and manages them as a unit for deployment, access control, and lifecycle management. Resource Pools (A) are a CPG concept for grouping cloud resources, not an ARM construct. Storage Accounts (B) store data but don't organize VM resources. Placement Groups (C) control VM placement within a datacenter for performance, not general resource organization.

questions.stem: Which Service in AWS is used to send alert messages to Cloud Provisioning and Governance?
questions.explanation: AWS Simple Notification Service (SNS) is used to send alert messages to Cloud Provisioning and Governance. SNS is AWS's pub/sub messaging service that pushes notifications to subscribers. CPG integrates with SNS topics to receive alerts about cloud resource state changes, billing thresholds, and CloudWatch alarms, enabling automated response within ServiceNow.

questions.stem: What objet does a Catalog Item utilize to dynamically set values for a Resource Block attribute?
questions.explanation: Expressions are the objects that catalog items use to dynamically set values for resource block attributes. Expressions can evaluate conditions, perform lookups against CMDB tables, and compute values at order time to populate resource block input parameters. This allows catalog items to be dynamic rather than static. Methods (A) are CAPI operations called by resource block steps. Functions (C) is a generic programming term, not a CPG component. Operations (D) define the actions a resource block can perform (provision, deprovision, etc.), not dynamic value setting.

questions.stem: When deploying an IIS Web Server in AWS for public access, which of the following must be configured to allow users to access the Web Server?

options.text: Security Group that allows inbound traffic
Network Traffic Group that allows inbound traffic

questions.explanation: To allow public access to an IIS Web Server in AWS, you must configure a Security Group that allows inbound traffic on the appropriate ports (HTTP 80, HTTPS 443). AWS Security Groups act as virtual firewalls controlling inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. A TLS Certificate (A) encrypts traffic but doesn't control access. Network Traffic Group (C) is not a standard AWS construct — the correct term is Security Group. Windows Host Based Firewall (D) is OS-level, but AWS traffic must first pass through the Security Group.
